slides.title: You blame your wrists.
slides.body: Bar sits in your palms, wrists scream, so you stretch your wrists. Nothing changes.

slides.title: Tight lats drop your elbows.
slides.body: Elbows sink, the bar rolls into your hands, and your wrists hold a load they were never built for.

slides.title: Fingertips, not fists.
slides.body: Two or three fingers under the bar is a real front rack. Shoulders hold it. Hands just steady it.

slides.title: Elbows high and forward.
slides.body: Point them at the wall in front of you. The bar sits on your shoulders, not your palms.

slides.title: Open the lats before you load.
slides.body: Two minutes of lat stretching, then a few slow front squats with an empty bar. Every time.

slides.title: Watch your elbows in the hole.
slides.body: If they drop at the bottom of a front squat, the bar tips forward and so do you.
